--- title: "Visual attention span: digits" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HVIS_CAP_VAten_NUMEROS_5" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (F · Span and memory; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HVIS_CAP_VAten_NUMEROS_5`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Amplitud visoatencional: números*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HVIS_CAP_VAten_NUMEROS_5.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Visual attention span: digits, from age 4 to 7 (4,607 administrations in 5 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .18. AUC .54–.69 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2002 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | brief visual presentation | | Items | 16 | | Task family | F · Span and memory | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | After the presentation of a fixation point for 200ms, a four-digit number appears on the center of the screen for 50/200 ss. The child is instructed to remember this number and to point which among three options corresponds to the given number. | ## Theoretical framework **Visual-attentional span** is the number of visual elements processed simultaneously within a string. On the platform, a string of letters, numbers or symbols is briefly presented and the child chooses what they saw. **Serial search** asks whether there is an O among groups of Qs of different sizes. The **sustained attention** task (UNED battery) consists of 50 trials in which the child decides whether the name they hear matches the picture; despite its name, the catalog describes it as an index of inhibitory control. Reading requires processing several letters at once and maintaining attention along the line. **What the evidence says:** - **Visual-attentional span predicts reading beyond phonemic awareness.** In 417 French children in Grades 1, 3 and 5, it predicted reading independently of phonemic awareness, especially for irregular words [@bosse2009span]. Orthographic depth modulates how this attention is distributed: advanced bilinguals reading in French and Basque distributed it more evenly than those reading in Spanish and Basque [@antzaka2018depth]. - **Visual search is associated with reading, with small samples.** In 16 children with dyslexia and 16 controls, slow serial search was associated with visual-attentional span and with irregular word reading, not with phonology [@lallier2013search]. Visual scanning measured in preschool predicted learning to read in Italian children [@ferretti2008scanning]. - **Sustained attention is related more to comprehension than to word reading.** In 245 poor readers in Grades 4 and 5, it explained unique variance in comprehension, but not in reading accuracy or fluency [@macdonald2021sustained]. The evidence is weaker than for phonological processes and there are almost no studies in Spanish. **What our data show.** - **Letter and symbol subtests.** With 6–10 points and a single session, AUC from .47 to .61: separately they are not interpretable. - **Numbers and letters (36 items, ages 4–5).** α = .60 and AUC of .66–.67 against persistent difficulty and of .65 against later low comprehension. It is the best in the family, as expected of alphanumeric stimuli. - **Numbers (16 items).** α = .56 and almost zero stability across school years (ρ = .05–.19). AUC from .54 to .69. - **Serial search.** α = .74, ceiling of 11–20% and AUC from .58 to .63. - **Sustained attention.** Despite an α of .95, it shows no validity: extreme ceiling (median 45 out of 50), stability of ρ = .03–.16, null correlation with the other domains and AUC from .43 to .56. It should not be used until the data have been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 2002| 2012| 157|2016/17 | 390| 386| 0| 17| | 5.1| 2002| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 319| 315| 0| 16| | 5.1| 4035| 2014| 896|2019/20 | 350| 13| 337| 21| | 5.2| 2002| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 893| 0| 893| 35| | 6.1| 2002| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 777| 0| 777| 31| | 6.1| 4036| 2013| 898|2019/20 | 557| 399| 158| 35| | 6.2| 2002| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 913| 265| 648| 34| | 7.3| 2002| 2010| 190|2017/18 | 408| 159| 249| 30| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 2002| 4.2| 386| 2012| 6.07| 2.20| 6| 0.44| 0.00| 0.00| | 2002| 5.1| 315| 2012| 6.67| 2.55| 7| 0.21| 0.63| 0.00| | 4036| 6.1| 399| 2013| 8.10| 2.82| 8| -0.35| 1.25| 0.25| | 2002| 6.2| 265| 2010| 8.13| 2.89| 8| -0.28| 0.00| 0.00| | 2002| 7.3| 159| 2010| 10.04| 2.21| 10| -0.34| 0.00| 0.00| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–16 correct responses. | Form| Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----:|----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 2002| 4.2| 386|1.9–11.2 |1–15 |0–16 | | | 2002| 5.1| 315|2–12 |0–15 |0–16 | | | 4036| 6.1| 399|0–14 |0–16 |0–16 | | | 2002| 6.2| 265|1–14 |1–14 |0–16 | | | 2002| 7.3| 159|5–15 |2–15 |0–16 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .05–.19 (median .18, 3 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .56. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 6.2| 7.3| 385| 0.19| 0.19| | 2011| 5.2| 6.1| 707| 0.17| 0.18| | 2012| 4.2| 5.1| 311| 0.09| 0.05| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.2, r = .10); Phonological awareness (5.1, r = .24); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .24); Phonological awareness (6.1, r = .36); Phonological awareness (6.2, r = .28); Word and text reading (7.3, r = .26). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .54–.69. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .54–.60. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_NUMEROS_5_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .54–.67 (4 time points; 127–416 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|----:| | 2002| 4.2| 386| 2012| 3| 3| 4| 5| 6| 7| 9.0| | 2002| 5.1| 315| 2012| 3| 4| 4| 5| 7| 8| 10.0| | 4035| 5.1| 350| 2014| 3| 3| 4| 5| 7| 8| 9.1| | 2002| 5.2| 893| 2011| 3| 4| 4| 5| 7| 9| 10.0| | 2002| 6.1| 777| 2011| 4| 5| 6| 7| 9| 10| 12.0| | 4036| 6.1| 399| 2013| 4| 4| 5| 6| 8| 10| 11.0| | 2002| 6.2| 265| 2010| 3| 4| 5| 6| 8| 10| 12.0| | 2002| 7.3| 159| 2010| 6| 7| 8| 9| 10| 12| 13.0| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_CAP_VAten_NUMEROS_5_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ### Forms: can they be pooled? Forms given at the same time point are compared. They are considered **equivalent** if the mean difference is smaller than 0.20 SD and the SD ratio is between 0.80 and 1.25. If the same children took them, **linear equating** is also computed, which puts the second form on the scale of the first, together with the correlation between forms (parallel-forms reliability). If the groups differ, the difference mixes form and cohort. | Time point| Form 1| Form 2|Comparison | d (2 − 1)| SD ratio|Verdict |r between forms |Equating | |----------:|------:|------:|:----------------|---------:|--------:|:----------|:---------------|:--------| | 5.1| 2002| 4035|different groups | -0.01| 0.96|equivalent |— |— | | 6.1| 2002| 4036|different groups | -0.18| 1.10|equivalent |— |— | ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 274| -0.003| 0.955| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 390| -0.065| 0.518| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 386| 0.009| 0.865| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 390| 0.028| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 594| -0.005| 0.908| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 638| -0.022| 0.785| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 651| 0.024| 0.549| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 669| 0.027| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 892| 0.107| 0.001| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 890| 0.009| 0.896| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 886| 0.076| 0.023| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 893| 0.056| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,321| 0.042| 0.127| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,329| 0.022| 0.681| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,327| 0.076| 0.006| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,334| 0.034| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 913| 0.162| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 911| -0.075| 0.259| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 910| 0.025| 0.459| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 913| 0.049| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.3| 408| 0.120| 0.016| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.3| 405| -0.090| 0.368| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.3| 405| 0.004| 0.931| |School (ICC) | 7.3| 408| 0.102| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Visual attention span: digits” (code 2002; LEEDUCA battery) assesses visual attention span. A string of visual stimuli is briefly presented and the child reports those seen. It comprises 16 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 8 sessions, from 4 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .56 (N = 4,140, 16 items). Stability across time points was ρ = .05–.19. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .54–.60. ## Pending issues - The task has 2 forms; in 0 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - Estabilidad muy baja entre aplicaciones (ρ = .12): revisar los datos (códigos, versiones o tiempos) antes de usar la tarea *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
